title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with a tomato-based sauce and added vegetables is a home recipe that combines whole‑grain noodles, a flavorful tomato sauce, and a mix of vegetables such as carrots, zucchini, and bell pepper. The dish is rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals, providing a steady release of energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains more fiber and protein than traditional white‑flour pasta.
Tomatoes are an excellent source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
Adding a variety of vegetables boosts the content of vitamins A, C, and B‑complex, as well as minerals like potassium and magnesium.
A homemade sauce lets you control salt and sugar levels, making the meal healthier.
Cooking tomatoes and vegetables over moderate heat preserves most of their nutrients.

items.title: High in Fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta and vegetables support healthy digestion and promote satiety.

items.title: Source of Complex Carbohydrates
items.content: The pasta provides a stable blood‑glucose level, offering sustained energy throughout the day.

items.title: Lycopene and Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes supply lycopene, which may reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and certain cancers.

items.title: Vitamins and Minerals
items.content: Vegetables add vitamins A, C, K and potassium, supporting heart and muscle function.

items.title: Low in Saturated Fat
items.content: The dish is prepared without butter or heavy cream, making it suitable for low‑saturated‑fat diets.

items.title: Gluten Sensitivity
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, so individuals with celiac disease or gluten intolerance should use a gluten‑free alternative.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: If the sauce is prepared with a lot of added salt, it may increase the risk of high blood pressure.

items.title: Tomato Acidity
items.content: People with gastritis or acid reflux may experience increased heartburn from tomato‑based sauces.

content.title: How to Prepare and Serve
content.content: Cook the whole grain pasta until al dente, drain, reserving a cup of pasta water. Sauté finely chopped vegetables in a pan, add the tomato sauce, and simmer for 10‑15 minutes, thinning with reserved water if needed. Toss the pasta with the sauce, optionally garnish with fresh herbs or grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Keep dry pasta separate in a cool, dry place; reheat with a splash of water on the stovetop or in the microwave.
